note: Clean pass with three caveats. (1) The source .sav (Mendeley 10.17632/3gx5f24fpv, the only file in the deposit) carries NO variable labels and no value labels for b1-b17 -- checked both levels -- so nothing at the source ties b<i> to an item; the item wording comes from the published Turkish form of the instrument (Yildirim & Ilhan 2010, Turk Psikiyatri Dergisi 21(4):301-308, Table 1, all 17 items printed and numbered), and b<i> = item <i> is an inference (mapping_basis=paper_order), tested in verify_kermen_2022_self_efficacy.R and recorded PARTIAL. (2) The 11 items the adaptation paper declares reverse-scored (2,4,5,6,7,10,11,12,14,16,17) are stored ALREADY REVERSED in this table: sum(b1..b17) reproduces the source paper's reported self-efficacy mean/SD of 61.54/9.75 exactly in the scored 17-85 metric, and all 17 corrected item-total correlations are positive (0.235-0.554), which is impossible if 11 items were raw. The shipped option_text is therefore reversed for those 11 items -- resp=1 carries the anchor 'cok iyi' and resp=5 'hic' -- so that the anchor named against each stored value is the one the respondent actually chose. (3) Only the two endpoints of the 5-point scale were labelled ('hic' ... 'cok iyi'); resp 2-4 ship blank option_text rather than being padded. Rights: no quotable restriction from the wording's rights holder. Sherer et al. (1982) is a Psychological Reports article whose SAGE 'request permissions' link is a notice about the article, not a term governing the instrument (the PANAS case); the Turkish adaptation was published open-access by Turk Psikiyatri Dergisi and states no reuse term. The TOAD scale directory's page for this scale carries only the site-wide boilerplate recommending that users contact the responsible author, which is a third-party directory's recommendation, not the holder's clause -- it reserves no right, so it does not block. No register row written (a round may never write ship/ship_with_note).
